facts.text: Daikin Park opened in 2000 as the home of the Houston Astros, while the Toyota Center began hosting the Rockets in 2003.
Sam Houston Park on Bagby Street houses the Houston Heritage Society, preserving historic houses that tell the city’s early story.
After the Galveston Hurricane of 1900, investors shifted to Downtown Houston, seeking a safer port location away from hurricane‑hit Galveston.
From 1971 to 2018, about forty Downtown buildings earned spots on the National Register of Historic Places, reflecting the area’s rich heritage.
Enron’s 40‑floor skyscraper, completed in 2002, stood as Houston’s tallest building until the company collapsed two years later.
Historically, Houston Industries and its subsidiary Houston Power & Lighting kept their headquarters in Downtown, shaping the city’s energy legacy.
